label: def: M-proto
title: Definition
body_md:
\label{def: M-proto}
Let $\ensuremath{\mathsf{C}}$ be a finitely complete category and $\ensuremath{\mathscr{M}}$ a class of morphisms of $\ensuremath{\mathsf{C}}$. We say that $\ensuremath{\mathsf{C}}$ satisfies the \emph{$\ensuremath{\mathscr{M}}$-version of protomodularity} when, for any morphism $h\colon Z\to Y$, the change-of-base functor $h^*\colon \ensuremath{\mathrm{Pt}}_Y(\ensuremath{\mathsf{C}})\to \ensuremath{\mathrm{Pt}}_Z(\ensuremath{\mathsf{C}})$ is conservative on $\ensuremath{\mathscr{M}}$.

label: diag: h*(m) iso
title: Proof
body_md:
For $\ensuremath{\mathscr{M}}=\ensuremath{\mathscr{M}\mathsf{or}}$ or $\ensuremath{\mathscr{M}}=\ensuremath{\mathscr{M}\mathsf{ono}}$ this result is the equivalence between (i) and (ii) of Theorem~\ref{thm: characterization of protomodularity}.\\
(i) $\Rightarrow$ (ii) We consider diagram~\eqref{diag:iv} with $K'=K$ and $Y'=Y$, so that the isomorphisms are the identity morphisms; suppose that $m\in\ensuremath{\mathscr{M}}$. This diagram shows that $0_Y^*(m)=1_K$ which, by assumption, implies that $m$ is an isomorphism.\\
(ii) $\Rightarrow$ (i) Consider an arbitrary morphism $h\colon Z\to Y$ of $\ensuremath{\mathsf{C}}$ and a morphism $m\colon X'\to X$ in $\ensuremath{\mathscr{M}}$ such that $h^*(m)=1_P$
\begin{equation}\label{diag: h*(m) iso}
	\vcenter{\xymatrix@R=30pt@C=50pt{P  \ar[rr]^-{\pi_{X'}}  \ar@{=}[dr]^-{\;h^*(m)=1_P} \ar@/_/@<-7pt>[ddr]_-{\pi_Z} & & X' \ar@/_/@<-2pt>[ddr]_(.25){f'} \ar[dr]^-{\;m\in \ensuremath{\mathscr{M}}}  \\
		& P \ar[rr]^(.4){\pi_{X}} \ar@<-2pt>[d]_-{\pi_Z} & & X \ar@<-2pt>[d]_(.3){f} \\
		& Z \ar@<-2pt>[u]_-{i_Z} \ar[rr]_-h \ar@/^/@<3pt>[uul]_-{i_Z} & & Y; \ar@<-2pt>[u]_(.7){s} \ar@/^/@<-2pt>[uul]_(.65){s'}}}
\end{equation}
here $P=Z\times_Y X=Z\times_Y X'$. By taking the kernel of $\pi_Z$ we get $\pi_{X'}\ker(\pi_Z)=\ker(f')$ and $\pi_{X}\ker(\pi_Z)=\ker(f)$
\[
\xymatrix@=25pt{ K \ar@{|>->}[r]^-{\ker(f')} \ar@{=}[d] & X' \ar@<2pt>[r]^-{f'} \ar[d]_-{m\in \ensuremath{\mathscr{M}}} & Y \ar@<2pt>[l]^-{s'} \ar@{=}[d] \\
		K \ar@{|>->}[r]_-{\ker(f)} & X \ar@<2pt>[r]^-f & Y, \ar@<2pt>[l]^-s}
\]
so that we can conclude that $m$ is an isomorphism, by assumption.

label: prop: M-proto iff orthogonal to M
title: Proposition
head: environment
labels: prop: M-proto iff orthogonal to M

title: Proof
body_md:
For $\ensuremath{\mathscr{M}}=\ensuremath{\mathscr{M}\mathsf{ono}}$ this result is the equivalence between (i) and (iii) of Theorem~\ref{thm: characterization of protomodularity}.\\
(i) $\Rightarrow$ (ii) To prove that $(\pi_X,s)$ is orthogonal to $\ensuremath{\mathscr{M}}$, we consider the commutative diagram
\[
	\xymatrix@=25pt{ & M \ar@{ >->}[d]|-{m\in \ensuremath{\mathscr{M}}} \\
		Z\times_Y X \ar[ur]^-a \ar[r]_-{\pi_X} & X & Y. \ar[ul]_-b \ar[l]^-s}
\]
This gives the commutative diagram
\[
	\xymatrix@R=30pt@C=50pt{Z\times_Y X  \ar[rr]^-{a}  \ar@{=}[dr]^-{\;h^*(m)=1_{Z\times_Y X}} \ar@/_/@<-7pt>[ddr]_-{\pi_Z} & & M \ar@/_/@<-2pt>[ddr]_(.25){fm} \ar@{ >->}[dr]^-{\;m\in \ensuremath{\mathscr{M}}}  \\
		& Z\times_Y X  \ar[rr]^(.4){\pi_{X}} \ar@<-2pt>[d]_-{\pi_Z} & & X \ar@<-2pt>[d]_(.3){f} \\
		& Z \ar@<-2pt>[u]_-{i_Z} \ar[rr]_-h \ar@/^/@<3pt>[uul]_-{i_Z} & & Y, \ar@<-2pt>[u]_(.7){s} \ar@/^/@<-2pt>[uul]_(.65){b}}
\]
where the front and top faces are pullbacks (the top face is a pullback since $m$ is a monomorphism). Note that $mai_Z =\pi_Xi_Z=sh=mbh$ implies that $a i_Z=bh$, since $m$ is a monomorphism. This proves that the back face commutes with respect to the sections. By assumption we may conclude that $m$ is an isomorphism.\\
(ii) $\Rightarrow$ (i) Consider diagram~\eqref{diag: h*(m) iso} with $m$ a monomorphism in $\ensuremath{\mathscr{M}}$. We get
\[
	\xymatrix@=25pt{ & X' \ar@{ >->}[d]|-{m\in \ensuremath{\mathscr{M}}} \\
		P \ar[ur]^-{\pi_X'} \ar[r]_-{\pi_X} & X & Y; \ar[ul]_-{s'} \ar[l]^-s}
\]
by assumption, $m$ is an isomorphism.

title: Proposition
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
For $\ensuremath{\mathscr{M}}=\ensuremath{\mathscr{M}\mathsf{or}}$ or $\ensuremath{\mathscr{M}}=\ensuremath{\mathscr{M}\mathsf{ono}}$ this result is the equivalence between (i) and (iv) of Theorem~\ref{thm: characterization of protomodularity}.\\
(i) $\Rightarrow$ (ii) Take the pullback of $(y,q)$ and the induced morphism $z$ in
\[
\xymatrix@R=25pt@C=35pt{X \ar@(r,u)[drr]^-{m\in \ensuremath{\mathscr{M}}} \ar@{.>}[dr]^-z \ar@(d,l)@<-2pt>[ddr]_-f  \\
	& Z \ar@{}[dr]|-{\framebox{\scriptsize\ensuremath{\mathrm{\mathrm{C}}}}} \ar@<-2pt>[d]_-{\pi_Y} \ar[r]^-{\pi_A}  
 \ar@{-}[]+R+<6pt,-1pt>;[]+RD+<6pt,-6pt> 
 \ar@{-}[]+D+<.5ex,-6pt>;[]+RD+<6pt,-6pt> & A \ar[d]^-q \\
	& Y \ar@<-2pt>@(l,d)[uul]_-s \ar@<-2pt>[u]_-{zs} \ar[r]_-y & B.}
\]
Note that $z\in \ensuremath{\mathscr{M}}$, because $\ensuremath{\mathscr{M}}$ is left-cancellative. We get
\[
\xymatrix@R=25pt@C=35pt{U \ar[r]^-{zu} \ar@<-2pt>[d]_-g \ar@{}[dr]|-{\framebox{\scriptsize\ensuremath{\mathrm{\mathrm{D}}}}} & Z \ar@{}[dr]|-{\framebox{\scriptsize\ensuremath{\mathrm{\mathrm{C}}}}}  
 \ar@{-}[]+R+<6pt,-1pt>;[]+RD+<6pt,-6pt> 
 \ar@{-}[]+D+<.5ex,-6pt>;[]+RD+<6pt,-6pt> \ar@<-2pt>[d]_-{\pi_Y} \ar[r]^-{\pi_A} & A \ar[d]^-q \\
	V \ar@<-2pt>[u]_-t \ar[r]_-v & Y \ar@<-2pt>[u]_-{zs} \ar[r]_-y & B,}
\]
where \framebox{\scriptsize\ensuremath{\mathrm{D}}}\framebox{\scriptsize\ensuremath{\mathrm{C}}}=\framebox{\scriptsize\ensuremath{\mathrm{A}}}\framebox{\scriptsize\ensuremath{\mathrm{B}}} and \framebox{\scriptsize\ensuremath{\mathrm{C}}} are pullbacks, so that \framebox{\scriptsize\ensuremath{\mathrm{D}}} is a pullback. This gives the following commutative diagram
\[
	\xymatrix@R=30pt@C=50pt{U  \ar[rr]^-{u}  \ar@{=}[dr]^-{\;v^*(z)=1_U} \ar@/_/@<-7pt>[ddr]_-{g} & & X \ar@/_/@<-2pt>[ddr]_(.25){f} \ar[dr]^-{\;z\in \ensuremath{\mathscr{M}}}  \\
		& U  
 \ar@{-}[]+R+<6pt,-1pt>;[]+RD+<6pt,-6pt> 
 \ar@{-}[]+D+<.5ex,-6pt>;[]+RD+<6pt,-6pt> \ar[rr]^(.4){zu} \ar@<-2pt>[d]_-{g} & & Z \ar@<-2pt>[d]_(.3){\pi_Y} \\
		& V \ar@<-2pt>[u]_-{t} \ar[rr]_-v \ar@/^/@<3pt>[uul]_-{t} & & Y, \ar@<-2pt>[u]_(.7){zs} \ar@/^/@<-2pt>[uul]_(.65){s}}
\]
from which we deduce that $z$ is an isomorphism; consequently \framebox{\scriptsize\ensuremath{\mathrm{B}}} is a pullback.\\
(ii) $\Rightarrow$ (i) Consider diagram~\eqref{diag: h*(m) iso}. We get
\[
	\xymatrix@R=25pt@C=35pt{ P \ar@(u,u)[rr]^-{\pi_X} \ar@<-2pt>[d]_-{\pi_Z} \ar[r]^-{\pi_{X'}} \ar@{}[dr]|-{\framebox{\scriptsize\ensuremath{\mathrm{\mathrm{A}}}}} & X' \ar@<-2pt>[d]_-{f'} \ar[r]^-{m\in \ensuremath{\mathscr{M}}} \ar@{}[dr]|-{\framebox{\scriptsize\ensuremath{\mathrm{\mathrm{B}}}}} & X \ar[d]^-f \\
	Z \ar@(d,d)[rr]_-{h} \ar@<-2pt>[u]_-{i_Z} \ar[r]_-h & Y \ar@<-2pt>[u]_-{s'} \ar@{=}[r]_-{1_Y} & Y,}
\]
where \framebox{\scriptsize\ensuremath{\mathrm{A}}} and \framebox{\scriptsize\ensuremath{\mathrm{A}}}\framebox{\scriptsize\ensuremath{\mathrm{B}}} are pullbacks, so that \framebox{\scriptsize\ensuremath{\mathrm{B}}} is also a pullback; thus $m$ is an isomorphism.

label: prop: pb pp for regular cat
title: Proposition

labels: prop: pb pp for regular cat

title: Proof
body_md:
For $\ensuremath{\mathscr{M}}=\ensuremath{\mathscr{M}\mathsf{or}}$ or $\ensuremath{\mathscr{M}}=\ensuremath{\mathscr{M}\mathsf{ono}}$ the proof of the equivalence between (i) and (ii) can be found in~\cite{NEKEAC}.\\
(i) $\Rightarrow$ (ii) Take vertical kernel pairs as in
	\[
	\xymatrix@R=30pt@C=35pt{ \ensuremath{\mathrm{Eq}}(g) \ar@{}[dr]|-{\framebox{\scriptsize\ensuremath{\mathrm{\mathrm{C}}}}} \ar[r]^-{\overline{u}} \ar@<-4pt>[d]_-{g_1} \ar@<4pt>[d]^-{g_2} & \ensuremath{\mathrm{Eq}}(f) \ar@{}[dr]|-{\framebox{\scriptsize\ensuremath{\mathrm{\mathrm{D}}}}} \ar[r]^-{\overline{m}} \ar@<-4pt>[d]_-{f_1} \ar@<4pt>[d]^-{f_2} & \ensuremath{\mathrm{Eq}}(q) \ar@<-4pt>[d]_-{q_1} \ar@<4pt>[d]^-{q_2}\\
	U \ar[u]  \ar@{>>}[d]_-{g} \ar[r]^-{u} \ar@{}[dr]|-{\framebox{\scriptsize\ensuremath{\mathrm{\mathrm{A}}}}} & X \ar[u] \ar@{>>}[d]_-{f} \ar[r]^-{m\in \ensuremath{\mathscr{M}}} \ar@{}[dr]|-{\framebox{\scriptsize\ensuremath{\mathrm{\mathrm{B}}}}} & A \ar[u]		\ar[d]^-q \\
	V \ar[r]_-v & Y \ar[r]_-y & B.}
	\]
Since \framebox{\scriptsize\ensuremath{\mathrm{A}}} and \framebox{\scriptsize\ensuremath{\mathrm{A}}}\framebox{\scriptsize\ensuremath{\mathrm{B}}} are pullbacks, then so are \framebox{\scriptsize\ensuremath{\mathrm{C}}} and \framebox{\scriptsize\ensuremath{\mathrm{C}}}\framebox{\scriptsize\ensuremath{\mathrm{D}}}. From properties (P2), (P3) and (P4), $(m\times m) \langle f_1,f_2\rangle=\langle q_1,q_2\rangle \overline{m}\in \ensuremath{\mathscr{M}}$; thus $\overline{m}\in \ensuremath{\mathscr{M}}$ by property (P1). We can apply Proposition~\ref{prop: pb pp} to \framebox{\scriptsize\ensuremath{\mathrm{C}}}\framebox{\scriptsize\ensuremath{\mathrm{D}}}, to conclude that \framebox{\scriptsize\ensuremath{\mathrm{D}}} is a pullback. By the Barr-Kock Theorem~\cite{Barr} we conclude that \framebox{\scriptsize\ensuremath{\mathrm{B}}} is a pullback as well.\\
(ii) $\Rightarrow$ (i) Follows immediately from Proposition~\ref{prop: pb pp}.

title: Remark
body_md: In the following sections we are mainly interested in studying $\ensuremath{\mathscr{M}}$-protomodularity for the classes of monomorphisms $\ensuremath{\mathscr{M}}=\ensuremath{\mathscr{SM}\mathsf{ono}}$, $\ensuremath{\mathscr{M}}=\ensuremath{\mathscr{S}\mathsf{pl}}$ the class of split monomorphisms and $\ensuremath{\mathscr{M}}=\ensuremath{\mathscr{PS}\mathsf{pl}}$ the class of protosplit monomorphisms (=kernels of split epimorphisms). $\ensuremath{\mathscr{SM}\mathsf{ono}}$ has the properties (P1)-(P4), so any of the above equivalences hold for $\ensuremath{\mathscr{SM}\mathsf{ono}}$-protomodular categories, as long as $\ensuremath{\mathsf{C}}$ satisfies their initial assumptions. $\ensuremath{\mathscr{S}\mathsf{pl}}$ has properties (P1)-(P3) but not (P4), so only the equivalences in Propositions~\ref{prop: M-proto iff SS5L for M}, \ref{prop: M-proto iff orthogonal to M} and \ref{prop: pb pp} hold for $\ensuremath{\mathscr{S}\mathsf{pl}}$-protomodular (pointed) categories. $\ensuremath{\mathscr{PS}\mathsf{pl}}$ only satisfies (P2); thus only the equivalences in Propositions~\ref{prop: M-proto iff SS5L for M} and \ref{prop: M-proto iff orthogonal to M} hold for $\ensuremath{\mathscr{S}\mathsf{pl}}$-protomodular pointed categories.

label: thm: F:CC->DD
title: Theorem
body_md: \label{thm: F:CC->DD} Consider finitely complete categories $\ensuremath{\mathsf{C}}$ and $\ensuremath{\mathsf{D}}$, with classes of morphisms $\ensuremath{\mathscr{M}}$ and $\ensuremath{\mathscr{N}}$, respectively. Let $F\colon \ensuremath{\mathsf{C}}\to \ensuremath{\mathsf{D}}$ be a  functor which preserves pullbacks, is conservative on $\ensuremath{\mathscr{M}}$ and such that $F(\ensuremath{\mathscr{M}})\subseteq\ensuremath{\mathscr{N}}$. If $\ensuremath{\mathsf{D}}$ is an $\ensuremath{\mathscr{N}}$-protomodular category, then $\ensuremath{\mathsf{C}}$ is an $\ensuremath{\mathscr{M}}$-protomodular category.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md: The proof is a straightforward adaptation of the well-known result concerning  ``ordinary'' protomodularity~\cite{NEKEAC}.

title: Corollary

title: Proof
body_md: A topological functor preserves limits and colimits, it is conservative on initial morphisms (see \cite{ST}), and every strong monomorphism is initial. Hence the statements of our corollary follow from the theorem above.

label: exe:Ord
title: Examples
body_md:
\label{exe:Ord}
It is well-known that:
\begin{itemize}
\item $\ensuremath{\mathsf{Set}}^\op$ is a (co)complete protomodular category~\cite{NEKEAC,BB};
\item the forgetful functors $\ensuremath{\mathsf{Top}}\to\ensuremath{\mathsf{Set}}$, $\ensuremath{\mathsf{Ord}}\to\ensuremath{\mathsf{Set}}$, and more generally $V\mbox{-}\ensuremath{\mathsf{Cat}}\to\ensuremath{\mathsf{Set}}$ (see \cite{CT}) are topological, therefore also $\ensuremath{\mathsf{Top}}^\op\to\ensuremath{\mathsf{Set}}^\op$, $\ensuremath{\mathsf{Ord}}^\op\to\ensuremath{\mathsf{Set}}^\op$, $(V\mbox{-}\ensuremath{\mathsf{Cat}})^\op\to\ensuremath{\mathsf{Set}}^\op$ are topological since the notion of topological functor is self-dual. (Here $\ensuremath{\mathsf{Top}}$ denotes the category of topological spaces and continuous maps, $\ensuremath{\mathsf{Ord}}$ denotes the category of preordered sets and monotone maps, and $V\mbox{-}\ensuremath{\mathsf{Cat}}$ denotes the category of $V$-categories and $V$-functors, for a commutative and unital quantale $V$.)
\end{itemize}
Hence Corollary \ref{cor:top} guarantees that $\ensuremath{\mathsf{Ord}}^\op,\;\ensuremath{\mathsf{Top}}^\op,\;(V\mbox{-}\ensuremath{\mathsf{Cat}})^\op$ are $\ensuremath{\mathscr{SM}\mathsf{ono}}$-protomodular.

None of the categories $\ensuremath{\mathsf{Top}}^\op$, $\ensuremath{\mathsf{Ord}}^\op$, and consequently $(V\mbox{-}\ensuremath{\mathsf{Cat}})^\op$ in general, are protomodular.
To prove this claim we give an example of a non-strong monomorphism $m$ with $h^*(m)$ isomorphism. We describe our diagram in $\ensuremath{\mathsf{Ord}}$, for simplicity. In the following diagram
\[
\xymatrix@=30pt{A \ar[r]^-h \ar@{ >->}@<-2pt>[d]_-\alpha & C \ar@{ >->}@<-2pt>[d]_-{\alpha'} \\ B  \ar[r]_-g \ar[d]_-m \ar@{>>}@<-2pt>[u]_-\beta & D  
 \ar@{-}[]+L+<-9pt,1pt>;[]+LU+<-9pt,9pt> 
 \ar@{-}[]+U+<-.5ex,9pt>;[]+LU+<-9pt,9pt> \ar@{>>}@<-2pt>[u]_-{\beta'} \ar[d]|-\cong \\ B' \ar[r] & D' }
\]
$A=\{x_1,x_2,y_1,y_2\}$ with $x_1\ge x_2\le y_2\ge y_1$,
$C=\{1,x_2,y_2\}$ with $1\geq x_2\le y_2\ge 1$, $B$ and $B'$ have as
underlying set $\{x_1,x_2,y_1,y_2,x_0, y_0\}$, the order on $B$ is given
by the order on $A$ together with $x_0\le x_1,\,y_1\le y_0$, and the
order on $B'$ has the extra relation $x_0\le y_0$. The morphism $h\colon
A\to C$ is defined by $h(x_1)=h(y_1)=1$, $h(x_2)=x_2$, $h(y_2)=y_2$. The
inclusions $\alpha\colon A\to B$, $\alpha'\colon C\to D$ are split monomorphisms,
with retractions $\beta\colon B\to A$, $\beta'\colon D\to C$ where both identify
$x_0$ with $x_1$ and $y_0$ with $y_1$. Now it is easy to check that the
bijection $m\colon B\to B'$ is not an isomorphism, although its pushout
along $g$ is an isomorphism, since the identification of $x_1$ and $y_1$
by $h$ implies that $x_0\le y_0$ in $D$.

label: ex: paratopological groups
title: Example
body_md:
\label{ex: paratopological groups}
It was shown in \cite{BC} that the category $\ensuremath{\mathsf{TopGrp}}$ of topological groups and continuous group homomorphisms is protomodular.  If in the definition of topological group we drop the continuity of the inversion map we end up with the notion of \emph{paratopological group}. Let $\ensuremath{\mathsf{PTopGrp}}$ be the category of paratopological groups and continuous group homomorphisms. It is a complete and cocomplete category, and the forgetful functor $\ensuremath{\mathsf{PTopGrp}}\to\ensuremath{\mathsf{Grp}}$ is topological; indeed the proof of topologicity of this functor uses the same arguments used to show that the forgetful functor $\ensuremath{\mathsf{TopGrp}}\to\ensuremath{\mathsf{Grp}}$ is topological. Hence, by Corollary \ref{cor:top}, $\ensuremath{\mathsf{PTopGrp}}$ is $\ensuremath{\mathscr{SM}\mathsf{ono}}$-protomodular.

However, in contrast to the case of $\ensuremath{\mathsf{TopGrp}}$, $\ensuremath{\mathsf{PTopGrp}}$ is not protomodular, showing that the inversion map of each group is essential for protomodularity.
Let us show that the Split Short Five Lemma fails.

Let $Y$ be the group $(\mathbb{R},+)$ equipped with the topology $\mathcal{T}_S$ of the Sorgenfrey line; that is, the topology having $\{[0,a[\,;\,a\in\mathbb{R},\,a>0\}$ as basic neighbourhoods of $0$. It is a paratopological group but not a topological group.

In $(\mathbb{R},+)\times(\mathbb{R},+)$ we may consider two different topologies: the product topology $\mathcal{T}_1=\mathcal{T}_S\times\mathcal{T}_S$, and $\mathcal{T}_2$ having as basic neighbourhoods of $0$
\[\{U_a=\mathbb{R}\times\,]0,a[\,\cup\,[0,a[\times\{0\}\,;\,a\in\mathbb{R},\,a>0\}.\]
It is straightforward to check that both make $\mathbb{R}\times\mathbb{R}$ a non-topological paratopological group.

Both $\mathcal{T}_1$ and $\mathcal{T}_2$ make the following split short exact sequence in $\ensuremath{\mathsf{Grp}}$
\[
	\xymatrix@=25pt{ Y \ar@{ >->}[r]^-{\langle 1,0\rangle}  & (\ensuremath{\mathbb{R}}\times \ensuremath{\mathbb{R}}, \mathcal{T}_i) \ar@<2pt>[r]^-{\pi_2}  & Y \ar@<2pt>[l]^-{\langle 0,1\rangle}}
\]
a split short exact sequence in $\ensuremath{\mathsf{PTopGrp}}$; indeed, as the product topology, the case of $\mathcal{T}_1$ clearly works. Let us check our claim for $\mathcal{T}_2$:
\begin{itemize}
\item $k=\langle 1,0\rangle$ is a strong monomorphism: $k^{-1}(U_a)=[0,a[$.
\item $s=\langle 0,1\rangle$ is continuous: $s^{-1}(U_a)=[0,a[$.
\item To show that $\pi_2$ is continuous it is enough to notice that $\pi_2$ is continuous in $0$, and this follows from $\pi_2(U_a)= [0,a[$.
\end{itemize}
Now, for each $a>0$, $U_a\supseteq [0,a[\times\,[0,a[$, hence $U_a$ is clearly a neighbourhood of $0$ in $\mathcal{T}_1$, which implies that the identity map $(\mathbb{R}\times\mathbb{R},\mathcal{T}_1)\to(\mathbb{R}\times\mathbb{R},\mathcal{T}_2)$ is continuous. Since it is not an isomorphism, this example shows that the Split Short Five Lemma fails.

body_md: \label{ex: Mon with M=isos and maps in Grp} In $\ensuremath{\mathsf{Mon}}$, consider the class of morphisms $\ensuremath{\mathscr{M}}$ to be all isomorphisms in $\ensuremath{\mathsf{Mon}}$ and all group homomorphisms. Then $\ensuremath{\mathsf{Mon}}$ is $\ensuremath{\mathscr{M}}$-protomodular. Indeed, consider diagram~\eqref{diag: def of h*} with $m$ a group homomorphism and $h^*(m)$ an isomorphism. Since $f$ is surjective, then $Y$ is also a group, so that the right face of this diagram lives in $\ensuremath{\mathsf{Grp}}$. The proof that $m$ is an isomorphism follows as in $\ensuremath{\mathsf{Grp}}$, since the only inverses we must take are in $X$ or $X'$.

label: prop: Spl-proto => h* reflects monos
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop: Spl-proto => h* reflects monos}
If $\ensuremath{\mathsf{C}}$ is $\ensuremath{\mathscr{S}\mathsf{pl}}$-protomodular, then every change-of-base functor $h^*$ reflects monomorphisms.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Consider diagram~\eqref{diag: def of h*} such that $h^*(m)$ is a monomorphism. We extend the diagram by taking kernel pairs of $h^*(m)$ and of $m$. Since the top part of diagram~\eqref{diag: def of h*} is a pullback, so are the following downward commutative squares
\[
\xymatrix@=25pt{ Z\times_Y X'                               
 \ar@{-}[]+R+<4pt,-3pt>;[]+RD+<4pt,-6pt> 
 \ar@{-}[]+D+<3pt,-6pt>;[]+RD+<4pt,-6pt> \ar@{=}[d] \ar[r] & \ensuremath{\mathrm{Eq}}(m) \ar@<-5pt>[d]_-{m_1} \ar@<5pt>[d]^-{m_2} \\ Z\times_Y X' \ar[r]_-{\pi_{X'}} & X'\ar[u]|-{s_0},}
\]
where $s_0=\langle 1_{X'},1_{X'}\rangle$. Consequently, the upward square is also a pullback. We get
\[
\xymatrix@R=30pt@C=50pt{Z\times_Y X'  \ar[rr]^-{\pi_{X'}}  \ar@{=}[dr]^-{h^*(s_0)=1_{Z\times_Y X'}} \ar@/_/@<-7pt>[ddr]_-{\pi'_Z} & & X' \ar@/_/@<-2pt>[ddr]_(.25){f'} \ar@{ >->}[dr]^-{s_0}  \\
		& Z\times_Y X' \ar[rr] \ar@<-2pt>[d]_-{\pi'_Z} & & \ensuremath{\mathrm{Eq}}(m) \ar@<-2pt>[d]_(.3){f'm_1} \\
		& Z \ar@<-2pt>[u]_-{i'_Z} \ar[rr]_-h \ar@/^/@<3pt>[uul]_-{i'_Z} & & Y. \ar@<-2pt>[u]_(.7){s_0s'} \ar@/^/@<-2pt>[uul]_(.65){s'}}
\]
Since $s_0$ is a split monomorphism such that $h^*(s_0)$ is an isomorphism, then $s_0$ is an isomorphism, by assumption. It easily follows that each $m_i$ is a isomorphism; thus $m$ is a monomorphism.

label: lem: h* reflects monos iff pbs reflect monos
title: Lemma
head: environment
labels: lem: h* reflects monos iff pbs reflect monos

title: Proof
body_md:
(ii) $\Rightarrow$ (i) Given diagram~\eqref{diag: def of h*} with $h^*(m)$ a monomorphism, we conclude that $m$ is a monomorphism since the top part of this diagram is a pullback in $\ensuremath{\mathsf{C}}$.\\
(i) $\Rightarrow$ (ii) Consider the following diagram where the bottom square is a pullback in $\ensuremath{\mathsf{C}}$, $m$ is a monomorphism and the top is obtain by taking vertical kernel pairs
\[
	\xymatrix@=25pt{ A \ar@{=}[d]  \ar[r] & \ensuremath{\mathrm{Eq}}(n) \ar@<-5pt>[d]_-{n_1} \ar@<5pt>[d]^-{n_2} \\ A \ar@{ >->}[d]_-m \ar[r]                               
 \ar@{-}[]+R+<4pt,-3pt>;[]+RD+<4pt,-6pt> 
 \ar@{-}[]+D+<3pt,-6pt>;[]+RD+<4pt,-6pt> & C \ar[d]^-n \ar[u]|-{s_0} \\ B \ar[r] & D;}
\]
here $s_0=\langle 1_C,1_C\rangle$. It follows that the downward top squares are pullbacks. This implies that $n_1\colon (n_1,s_0)\to (1_C,1_C)$ is a morphism in $\ensuremath{\mathrm{Pt}}_C(\ensuremath{\mathsf{C}})$ such that $f^*(n_1)=1_A$. By assumption, $n_1$ is a monomorphism, which implies it is an isomorphism in $\ensuremath{\mathsf{C}}$ (since it is also a split epimorphism). It easily follows that $n$ is a monomorphism.
head: environment

label: cor: pointed + Spl-proto => (ker f=0 => f mono)
title: Corollary
body_md:
\label{cor: pointed + Spl-proto => (ker f=0 => f mono)}
Let $\ensuremath{\mathsf{C}}$ be a pointed $\ensuremath{\mathscr{S}\mathsf{pl}}$-protomodular category. If $\ker(n\colon C\to D)=0$, then $n$ is a monomorphism.
head: environment
labels: cor: pointed + Spl-proto => (ker f=0 => f mono)

title: Proof
body_md: This easily follows by combining Proposition~\ref{prop: Spl-proto => h* reflects monos} and Lemma~\ref{lem: h* reflects monos iff pbs reflect monos}.
head: environment

title: Remark
body_md: It is well-known that in every protomodular category pullbacks reflect monomorphisms~\cite{NEKEAC}. We do not know whether the equivalent properties of Lemma~\ref{lem: h* reflects monos iff pbs reflect monos} characterise $\ensuremath{\mathscr{S}\mathsf{pl}}$-protomodular categories.
head: environment

label: ex: Mon is not Spl-proto
title: Example
body_md: \label{ex: Mon is not Spl-proto} $\ensuremath{\mathsf{Mon}}$ is not a $\ensuremath{\mathscr{S}\mathsf{pl}}$-protomodular category since there exist monoid homomorphisms with trivial kernel that are not monomorphisms. So, we find pullbacks that do not reflect monomorphisms (see Corollary~\ref{cor: pointed + Spl-proto => (ker f=0 => f mono)}).

label: lem: M-proto for Nil_c
title: Lemma
head: environment
labels: diag: M-proto in C^op with kernels

title: Proof
body_md: Immediate from diagram~\eqref{diag: main in SAC} and the fact that $\ensuremath{\mathrm{Ker}}(e)=0$ implies that (the cokernel) $e$ is a monomorphism, since $\ensuremath{\mathsf{C}}$ is a protomodular category. Thus, $e$ is an isomorphism.
head: environment

label: lem: Ker(beta) and Ker(u) in [B,B]
title: Lemma
body_md: \label{lem: Ker(beta) and Ker(u) in [B,B]} Under the conditions of Lemma~\ref{lem: M-proto for Nil_c} applied to $\ensuremath{\mathsf{C}}=\ensuremath{\mathsf{Grp}}$ or $\ensuremath{\mathsf{C}}=\ensuremath{\mathsf{Nil}}_c$, we have $\ensuremath{\mathrm{Ker}}(\beta)\cap \ensuremath{\mathrm{Ker}}(u)\subseteq [B,B]$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
We give the proof for $\ensuremath{\mathsf{C}}=\ensuremath{\mathsf{Grp}}$; the proof for $\ensuremath{\mathsf{C}}=\ensuremath{\mathsf{Nil}}_c$ is similar. The abelianisation functor preserves the pushout~\eqref{diag: po of split mono} (since it is a left adjoint), so that
\[
	\xymatrix@=35pt{A^\ensuremath{\mathrm{ab}} \ar[r]^-{h^\ensuremath{\mathrm{ab}}} \ar@{ >->}@<-2pt>[d]_-{\alpha^\ensuremath{\mathrm{ab}}} & C^\ensuremath{\mathrm{ab}} \ar@{ >->}@<-2pt>[d]_-{\alpha'^\ensuremath{\mathrm{ab}}} \\ B^\ensuremath{\mathrm{ab}}  \ar[r]_-{u^\ensuremath{\mathrm{ab}}} \ar@{>>}@<-2pt>[u]_-{\beta^\ensuremath{\mathrm{ab}}} & D^\ensuremath{\mathrm{ab}},
		 
 \ar@{-}[]+L+<-9pt,1pt>;[]+LU+<-9pt,9pt> 
 \ar@{-}[]+U+<-.5ex,9pt>;[]+LU+<-9pt,9pt> \ar@{>>}@<-2pt>[u]_-{\beta'^\ensuremath{\mathrm{ab}}} }
\]
is a pushout in $\ensuremath{\mathsf{Ab}}$. It is easy to check that the kernel of $\beta^\ensuremath{\mathrm{ab}}$ is isomorphic to the reflection $\eta_B$ restricted to $\ensuremath{\mathrm{Ker}}(\beta)$; call it $K$. This leads to the isomorphic split short exact sequence in $\ensuremath{\mathsf{Ab}}$
\[
	\xymatrix@=25pt{ \ensuremath{\mathrm{Ker}}(\beta^\ensuremath{\mathrm{ab}}) \ar@{|>->}[r]^-{\ker(\beta^\ensuremath{\mathrm{ab}})} \ar@{=}[d] & B^\ensuremath{\mathrm{ab}} \ar@<2pt>@{>>}[r]^-{\beta^\ensuremath{\mathrm{ab}}} \ar[d]|-\cong & A^\ensuremath{\mathrm{ab}} \ar@<2pt>@{ >->}[l]^-{\alpha^\ensuremath{\mathrm{ab}}} \ar@{=}[d]\\
	\ensuremath{\mathrm{Ker}}(\beta^\ensuremath{\mathrm{ab}}) \ar[d]|-{\cong} \ar@{|>->}[r]_-{\langle 1,0\rangle} & \ensuremath{\mathrm{Ker}}(\beta^\ensuremath{\mathrm{ab}})\oplus A^\ensuremath{\mathrm{ab}} \ar[d]|-\cong \ar@<2pt>@{>>}[r]^-{\pi_2} & A^\ensuremath{\mathrm{ab}} \ar@{=}[d] \ar@<2pt>@{ >->}[l]^-{\langle 0,1\rangle} \\
	K \ar@{|>->}[r]_-{\langle 1,0\rangle} & K\oplus A^\ensuremath{\mathrm{ab}} \ar@<2pt>@{>>}[r]^-{\pi_2} & A^\ensuremath{\mathrm{ab}}.\ar@<2pt>@{ >->}[l]^-{\langle 0,1\rangle} }
\]
Then, the downward pushout from above may be simplified to
\[
	\xymatrix@R=25pt@C=35pt{A^\ensuremath{\mathrm{ab}} \ar[r]^-{h^\ensuremath{\mathrm{ab}}} \ar@{|>->}[d]_-{\langle 0,1\rangle} & C^\ensuremath{\mathrm{ab}} \ar@{|>->}[d]^-{\langle 0,1\rangle} \\ K\oplus A^\ensuremath{\mathrm{ab}}  \ar[r]_-{1_K\oplus h^\ensuremath{\mathrm{ab}}} & K\oplus C^\ensuremath{\mathrm{ab}}.  
 \ar@{-}[]+L+<-9pt,1pt>;[]+LU+<-9pt,9pt> 
 \ar@{-}[]+U+<-.5ex,9pt>;[]+LU+<-9pt,9pt>}
\]
Now we prove that $\ensuremath{\mathrm{Ker}}(\beta)\cap \ensuremath{\mathrm{Ker}}(u)\subseteq [B,B]$. Given $x\in \ensuremath{\mathrm{Ker}}(\beta)\cap \ensuremath{\mathrm{Ker}}(u)$, we have $\eta_B(x)\in K$. On the other hand, $u^\ensuremath{\mathrm{ab}}(\eta_B(x))=\eta_D(u(a))=0$. Using the fact that $u^\ensuremath{\mathrm{ab}}\cong 1_K\oplus h^\ensuremath{\mathrm{ab}}$, this last equality is equivalent to $1_K\oplus h^\ensuremath{\mathrm{ab}}(\eta_B(x),0)=(0,0)$, from which we conclude that $\eta_B(x)=0$; thus $x\in [B,B]$.
head: environment

label: ex: Nil_c^op
title: Example
body_md:
\label{ex: Nil_c^op} We show that $\ensuremath{\mathsf{Nil}}_c^\op$ is $\ensuremath{\mathscr{S}\mathsf{pl}}$-protomodular and $\ensuremath{\mathscr{PS}\mathsf{pl}}$-protomodular, where $\ensuremath{\mathscr{PS}\mathsf{pl}}$ denotes the class of protosplit monomorphisms, i.e. kernels of split epimorphisms. We also show that $\ensuremath{\mathsf{Nil}}_c^\op$ is not $\ensuremath{\mathscr{SM}\mathsf{ono}}$-protomodular. Since $\ensuremath{\mathsf{Nil}}_c$ is a semi-abelian variety, $\ensuremath{\mathsf{Nil}}_c^\op$ is finitely complete.\\
\noindent\textbf{$\ensuremath{\mathsf{Nil}}_c^\op$ is $\ensuremath{\mathscr{S}\mathsf{pl}}$-protomodular}\\
In this case the morphisms $e\in\ensuremath{\mathscr{M}}^\op$ as in diagram~\eqref{diag: main in SAC} are split epimorphisms. In $\ensuremath{\mathsf{Nil}}_c$ (and also in $\ensuremath{\mathsf{Grp}}$) it is easy to check that a quotient $e$ admits a splitting if and only if $\ensuremath{\mathrm{Ker}}(e)$ admits a complement in $B$, i.e. a subgroup $H\le B$ such that $\ensuremath{\mathrm{Ker}}(e)\cap H=0$ and $B=\ensuremath{\mathrm{Ker}}(e)H$.  By Lemma~\ref{lem: M-proto for Nil_c}, we must prove that for any pushout of type~\eqref{diag: po of split mono} and split epimorphism $e\in \ensuremath{\mathscr{M}}^\op$, we have
\[
	\left( \,\ensuremath{\mathrm{Ker}}(e) \subseteq \ensuremath{\mathrm{Ker}}(\beta)\cap \ensuremath{\mathrm{Ker}}(u) \,\right) \;\;\Rightarrow\;\; \ensuremath{\mathrm{Ker}}(e)=0.
\]
We know that $\ensuremath{\mathrm{Ker}}(e)$ admits a complement $H$ in $B$ and $\ensuremath{\mathrm{Ker}}(e) \subseteq [B,B]$ by Lemma~\ref{lem: Ker(beta) and Ker(u) in [B,B]}. We get
\[
	B=\ensuremath{\mathrm{Ker}}(e)H\subseteq [B,B]H\subseteq B \;\; \Rightarrow\;\; B=[B,B]H \;\; \Rightarrow\;\; H=B.
\]
The last implication only holds in $\ensuremath{\mathsf{Nil}}_c$. By induction on $c$ one can prove that, if $B$ is a nilpotent group of class $c$ and $H\le B$ such that $B=[B,B]H$, then $B=H$. To finish, $\ensuremath{\mathrm{Ker}}(e)=\ensuremath{\mathrm{Ker}}(e)\cap B=\ensuremath{\mathrm{Ker}}(e)\cap H=0$.

\noindent\textbf{$\ensuremath{\mathsf{Nil}}_c^\op$ is $\ensuremath{\mathscr{PS}\mathsf{pl}}$-protomodular}\\
In this case $e$ is the cokernel of a split monomorphism $i$ (with retraction $r$), whose kernel $\langle\langle Q\rangle\rangle$ is the normal closure of $Q$ in $B$. We consider $i$ to be an inclusion
\[
	\xymatrix@R=15pt@C=35pt{ \langle\langle Q\rangle\rangle \ar@{ |>->}[rr]^-{\ker(e)}  && B \ar@{|>}[r]^-{e=\ensuremath{\mathrm{coker}}(i)} \ar@<-2pt>@{>>}[dl]_-r & B/\langle\langle Q \rangle\rangle.\\ & Q \ar@{.>}[ul] \ar@<-2pt>@{_{(}->}[ur]_-i}
\]
Suppose that $\langle\langle Q\rangle\rangle \subseteq \ensuremath{\mathrm{Ker}}(\beta)\cap \ker(u)$. By Lemma~\ref{lem: Ker(beta) and Ker(u) in [B,B]}, $\langle\langle Q\rangle\rangle\subseteq[B,B]$. Considering $Q$ a subgroup of $B$, we have
\[
	Q=r(Q)\subseteq r(\langle\langle Q\rangle\rangle) \subseteq r([B,B])=[r(B),r(B)]=[Q,Q]\subseteq Q.
\]
We conclude that $Q=[Q,Q]$, i.e. it is a perfect (nilpotent) group. Up to this point, our arguments hold both in $\ensuremath{\mathsf{Nil}}_c$ and in $\ensuremath{\mathsf{Grp}}$. If $
Q$ is a nilpotent group of class $c$, then $0=\gamma_{c+1}(Q)=\gamma_c(Q)=\cdots =\gamma_1(Q)=Q$; thus $\langle\langle Q\rangle\rangle=0$. \\
\noindent\textbf{$\ensuremath{\mathsf{Nil}}_c^\op$ is not $\ensuremath{\mathscr{SM}\mathsf{ono}}$-protomodular}\\
In this case $e$ is just a strong epimorphism, and taking its kernel gives a short exact sequence (with no extra conditions on the basic setting of diagram~\eqref{diag: main in SAC}). In particular, we can consider a pushout~\eqref{diag: po of split mono} where $u$ is a strong epimorphism and take $e\colon \xymatrix@=10pt{B \ar@{|>}[r] &  A\, {}^B\!+ D}$ to be the diagonal (strong epimorphism) of the pushout of $(u,\beta)$. This implies that $\ensuremath{\mathrm{Ker}}(e)=\ensuremath{\mathrm{Ker}}(\beta)\cap\ensuremath{\mathrm{Ker}}(u)$. If $\ensuremath{\mathsf{Nil}}_c^\op$ is $\ensuremath{\mathscr{SM}\mathsf{ono}}$-protomodular, then $\ensuremath{\mathrm{Ker}}(e)=0$. However, this is not true in general. For example, in the pushout~\eqref{diag: po of split mono}, take $B=D_4=\langle r,s: r^4=s^2=1, srs=r^{-1}\rangle$ the diedral group of order 8 (which is nilpotent of class 2), $A=\langle s\rangle$, $C=0$ and $\alpha$ the inclusion. In this setting, $u$ is the cokernel of $\alpha$, so that $u\colon D_4\rightarrow D_4/\langle\langle s\rangle\rangle$, with $\langle\langle s\rangle \rangle=\{1,s,r^2,r^2s\}$. Consider the normal subgroup $L=\{1,r^2,rs,r^3s\}$ (because it has order 4 in a group of order 8) and define $\beta\colon D_4\to \langle s\rangle$ by $\beta(L)=\{1\}$ and $\beta(D_4\backslash L)=\{s\}$. We have $\ensuremath{\mathrm{Ker}}(\beta)\cap \ensuremath{\mathrm{Ker}}(u)=L\cap \langle\langle s\rangle\rangle=\{1,r^2\}\neq 0$.

title: Definition

label: def: M-Mal'tsev
title: Definition
body_md: \label{def: M-Mal'tsev} Let $\ensuremath{\mathsf{C}}$ be a category with binary products and $\ensuremath{\mathscr{M}}$ a class of monomorphisms of $\ensuremath{\mathsf{C}}$. We call $\ensuremath{\mathsf{C}}$ an \emph{$\ensuremath{\mathscr{M}}$-Mal'tsev category} when any relation $X\stackrel{d_1}{\longleftarrow} D \stackrel{d_2}{\longrightarrow} Y$ in $\ensuremath{\mathscr{M}}$ is difunctional.
head: environment

label: ex: M-Mal'tsev cats
title: Example
head: environment

label: prop: M-proto => Pt_Y(CC) is unital
title: Proposition
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Since the total and right diagrams in
\[
	\xymatrix@=25pt{X \ar[r]^-{i_X} \ar@<-2pt>[d]_-f \ar@(u,u)[rr]^-{1_X} & Z\times_Y X \ar@<-2pt>[d]_-{\pi_Z} \ar[r]^-{\pi_X} & X\ar@<-2pt>[d]_-f \\
		Y \ar@<-2pt>[u]_-s \ar[r]_-t \ar@(d,d)[rr]_-{1_Y} & Z \ar@<-2pt>[u]_-{i_Z} \ar[r]_-h & Y \ar@<-2pt>[u]_-s}
\]
are pullbacks, then so is the left diagram. The result follows by Proposition~\ref{prop: M-proto iff orthogonal to M}.
head: environment

label: prop: Pt_Y(CC) unital <=> M-Mal'tsev
title: Proposition
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
(i) $\Rightarrow$ (ii) Consider the relations as in~\eqref{eq: difunctional with relations}. We take the following pullbacks, and induced morphism $\lambda\colon W\to P$
\[
\xymatrix@=25pt{ W \ar@{.>}[dr]^-{\lambda} \ar@(r,u)[drr]^-{\langle \langle u,y\rangle, \langle u,v\rangle \rangle} \ar@(d,l)[ddr]_-{\langle \langle x,y \rangle, \langle u,y\rangle \rangle}\\
	& P \ar@{}[dr]|-{\framebox{\scriptsize\ensuremath{\mathrm{A}}}}                               
 \ar@{-}[]+R+<4pt,-3pt>;[]+RD+<4pt,-6pt> 
 \ar@{-}[]+D+<3pt,-6pt>;[]+RD+<4pt,-6pt> \ar@<-2pt>[d]_-{p_1} \ar@<2pt>[r]^-{p_2} & \ensuremath{\mathrm{Eq}}(d_1)                               
 \ar@{-}[]+R+<4pt,-3pt>;[]+RD+<4pt,-6pt> 
 \ar@{-}[]+D+<3pt,-6pt>;[]+RD+<4pt,-6pt>\ar@<-2pt>[d]_-{d_{11}} \ar@<2pt>[r]^-{d_{12}} \ar@<2pt>[l]^-{i_2} & D \ar[d]^-{d_1} \ar@<2pt>[l]^-{s_1}\\
	& \ensuremath{\mathrm{Eq}}(d_2)                               
 \ar@{-}[]+R+<4pt,-3pt>;[]+RD+<4pt,-6pt> 
 \ar@{-}[]+D+<3pt,-6pt>;[]+RD+<4pt,-6pt> \ar@<-2pt>[d]_-{d_{21}} \ar@<2pt>[r]^-{d_{22}} \ar@<-2pt>[u]_-{i_1}  & D \ar[r]_-{d_1} \ar[d]^-{d_2} \ar@<-2pt>[u]_-{s_1} \ar@<2pt>[l]^-{s_2} & X \\
	& D \ar@<-2pt>[u]_-{s_2} \ar[r]_-{d_2} & Y.
}
\]Next we take the pullback of $\langle d_1,d_2\rangle$ along $\langle d_1 d_{21}p_1, d_2d_{12}p_2\rangle$, which is a monomorphism in $\ensuremath{\mathscr{M}}$ by property (P5), and the induced morphisms $\alpha\colon \ensuremath{\mathrm{Eq}}(d_2)\to Q$, $\beta\colon \ensuremath{\mathrm{Eq}}(d_1)\to Q$
\[
	\xymatrix@R=25pt@C=30pt{\ensuremath{\mathrm{Eq}}(d_2) \ar@{.>}[dr]^-{\alpha} \ar@(r,u)[drrr]^-{d_{21}} \ar@(d,l)[ddr]_-{i_1} \\
		& Q                               
 \ar@{-}[]+R+<4pt,-3pt>;[]+RD+<4pt,-6pt> 
 \ar@{-}[]+D+<3pt,-6pt>;[]+RD+<4pt,-6pt> \ar[rr]^-{q} \ar@{ >->}[d]_-{\mu\in \ensuremath{\mathscr{M}}} && D \ar@{ >->}[d]^-{\langle d_1,d_2\rangle\in \ensuremath{\mathscr{M}}} \\
		& P \ar[rr]_-{\langle d_1 d_{21}p_1, d_2d_{12}p_2\rangle} && X\times Y
	}
		\xymatrix@R=25pt@C=30pt{\ensuremath{\mathrm{Eq}}(d_1) \ar@{.>}[dr]^-{\beta} \ar@(r,u)[drrr]^-{d_{12}} \ar@(d,l)[ddr]_-{i_2} \\
		& Q                               
 \ar@{-}[]+R+<4pt,-3pt>;[]+RD+<4pt,-6pt> 
 \ar@{-}[]+D+<3pt,-6pt>;[]+RD+<4pt,-6pt> \ar[rr]^-{q} \ar@{ >->}[d]_-{\mu\in \ensuremath{\mathscr{M}}} && D \ar@{ >->}[d]^-{\langle d_1,d_2\rangle\in \ensuremath{\mathscr{M}}} \\
		& P \ar[rr]_-{\langle d_1 d_{21}p_1, d_2d_{12}p_2\rangle} && X\times Y.
	}
\]
Since \framebox{\scriptsize\ensuremath{\mathrm{A}}} is a pullback of points, then $(i_1,i_2)$ is orthogonal to $\ensuremath{\mathscr{M}}$ by assumption. From the commutativity of
\[
	\xymatrix@=25pt{ & Q \ar@{ >->}[d]|-{\mu\in \ensuremath{\mathscr{M}}} \\
		\ensuremath{\mathrm{Eq}}(d_2) \ar[ur]^-{\alpha}\ar[r]_-{i_1} & P & \ensuremath{\mathrm{Eq}}(d_1) \ar[l]^-{i_2} \ar[lu]_-{\beta}}
\]
we conclude that $\mu$ is an isomorphism. We then have $\langle d_1,d_2\rangle q\mu^{-1}\lambda = \langle x,v\rangle$, which proves that $xDv$.\\
(ii) $\Rightarrow$ (i) Consider the pullback of points below and a monomorphism $m\in\ensuremath{\mathscr{M}}$ such that $m\alpha=i_Z$ and $m\beta=i_X$ in
\[
	\xymatrix@=25pt{M \ar@{ >->}[dr]^-{m\in \ensuremath{\mathscr{M}}}   \\
		& Z\times_Y X \ar@<-2pt>[d]_-{\pi_Z} \ar@<2pt>[r]^-{\pi_X}                               
 \ar@{-}[]+R+<4pt,-3pt>;[]+RD+<4pt,-6pt> 
 \ar@{-}[]+D+<3pt,-6pt>;[]+RD+<4pt,-6pt> & X \ar@(u,r)[ull]_-{\beta} \ar@<-2pt>[d]_-f \ar@<2pt>[l]^-{i_X} \\
		& Z \ar@(l,d)[uul]^-{\alpha} \ar@<-2pt>[u]_-{i_Z} \ar@<2pt>[r]^-h & Y, \ar@<-2pt>[u]_-s \ar@<2pt>[l]^-t}
\]
By (P2) and (P4) it follows that $\langle \pi_Zm,\pi_Xm\rangle\colon M\rightarrowtail Z\times X$ is in $\ensuremath{\mathscr{M}}$; let us denote this relation by $M$. It is easy to check that
\[
\begin{array}{lll}
	\langle \pi_Z m, \pi_X m\rangle \alpha \pi_Z= \langle \pi_Z,sh\pi_Z \rangle & \Rightarrow & \;\;\;\;\pi_Z \,M\, sh\pi_Z, \\
	\langle \pi_Z m, \pi_X m\rangle \alpha t f \pi_X= \langle t f \pi_X, sh\pi_Z\rangle & \Rightarrow & tf \pi_X \,M\, sh\pi_Z, \\
	\langle \pi_Z m, \pi_X m\rangle \beta \pi_X= \langle tf\pi_X,\pi_X \rangle & \Rightarrow & tf \pi_X \,M\, \pi_X.
\end{array}
\]
                                                                                                                       
By difunctionality of $M$ we get $\pi_Z \, M\, \pi_X$, from which we conclude that $m$ is an isomorphism.

label: def: Ord-proto
title: Definition
body_md:
\label{def: Ord-proto}
Let $\ensuremath{\mathbb{C}}$ be a finitely complete $\ensuremath{\mathsf{Ord}}$-category. We call $\ensuremath{\mathbb{C}}$ an \emph{$\ensuremath{\mathsf{Ord}}$-protomodular category} when, for any morphism $h\colon Z\to Y$, the change-of-base functor $h^*\colon \ensuremath{\mathrm{Pt}}_Y(\ensuremath{\mathbb{C}})\to \ensuremath{\mathrm{Pt}}_Z(\ensuremath{\mathbb{C}})$ is conservative on the class of ff-monomorphisms of $\ensuremath{\mathbb{C}}$.
head: environment

label: lem: proto => Ord-proto
title: Lemma
body_md: \label{lem: proto => Ord-proto} If $\ensuremath{\mathsf{C}}$ is a protomodular category, then any $\ensuremath{\mathsf{Ord}}$-enrichment of $\ensuremath{\mathsf{C}}$ is an $\ensuremath{\mathsf{Ord}}$-pro\-to\-mo\-du\-lar category.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md: As mentioned earlier, $\ensuremath{\mathsf{C}}$ is protomodular if and only if any change-of-base functor is conservative on monomorphisms. In particular, they are conservative on ff-monomorphisms.
head: environment

title: Remark
body_md: Propositions~\ref{prop: M-proto iff SS5L for M}, \ref{prop: M-proto iff orthogonal to M} and \ref{prop: pb pp} hold in the context of $\ensuremath{\mathsf{Ord}}$-categories, where $\ensuremath{\mathscr{M}}$ is the class of ff-monomorphisms. Propositions~\ref{prop: pb pp for regular cat} and~\ref{prop: regular M-proto iff S5L for M} hold for any (pointed) regular $\ensuremath{\mathsf{Ord}}$-category with 2-pullbacks, so that 2-pullbacks and pullbacks coincide. Similarly, Proposition~\ref{prop: M-proto => Pt_Y(CC) is unital} holds for any $\ensuremath{\mathsf{Ord}}$-protomodular category and Proposition~\ref{prop: Pt_Y(CC) unital <=> M-Mal'tsev} for any $\ensuremath{\mathsf{Ord}}$-category with 2-pullbacks (again, so that 2-pullbacks and pullbacks coincide). Note that the assumptions (P1)--(P5) on morphisms needed for some of these results from Section~\ref{sec: M-protomodularity} and Section~\ref{sec: M-proto vs M-Mal'tsev} to hold, are replaced by the properties (F1)--(F5) on ff-monomorphisms listed below, which are easily seen to be always true in the context of $\ensuremath{\mathsf{Ord}}$-categories with 2-pullbacks.
head: environment

label: pps for ff-ms
title: Lemma
head: environment

title: Remark
body_md: The category $\ensuremath{\mathsf{Ord}}^\op$, with its natural $\ensuremath{\mathsf{Ord}}$-enrichment given, for morphisms $f,g\colon X\to Y$, by $f\le g$ if $f(y)\le g(y)$ for all $y\in Y$ is not $\ensuremath{\mathsf{Ord}}$-protomodular. As we have seen in Example \ref{exe:Ord}, $\ensuremath{\mathsf{Ord}}^\op$ is an $\ensuremath{\mathscr{SM}\mathsf{ono}}$-protomodular category which is not protomodular. In this enriched context, ff-monomorphisms coincide with monomorphisms (that is, surjective monotone maps in $\ensuremath{\mathsf{Ord}}$), not with strong monomorphisms, hence $\ensuremath{\mathsf{Ord}}$-protomodularity fails because protomodularity fails.
